description: Define an AWS Lambda–based HTTP and event-triggered API surface backed by DynamoDB for scalable key-value and document access patterns. Emphasize serverless scaling, API Gateway integration, SQS dead-letter paths for async triggers, and secure access via IAM roles and least-privilege policies — no long-lived access keys in function configuration.
constraints: DynamoDB access must honor least-privilege IAM policies; partition keys documented per table.
API Gateway routes must not expose unauthenticated mutating endpoints unless explicitly gated.
No plaintext storage of secrets — use Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store with rotation.
requiredCapabilities: AWS Lambda for HTTP APIs and asynchronous queue/event processing
Amazon DynamoDB as primary scalable data store
Amazon SQS or EventBridge for asynchronous command and integration patterns
CloudWatch and X-Ray for cold start latency, failures, and dependency calls
assumptions: Traffic can burst; cost controls (concurrency caps, alerting) must be articulated alongside scale-out behavior.
Clients tolerate at-least-once delivery semantics for async paths with idempotent handlers.
topologyHints: DynamoDB tables partitioned by tenant or aggregate root to contain hot partitions.
Separate HTTP façade functions from durable background processors driven from queues.
securityBaselineHints: VPC-attached Lambdas and private API Gateway integrations where policy requires confined data-plane paths.
IAM Access Analyzer and GuardDuty recommendations tracked as operational backlog items.
